title: Phone terminal view — typing straight into Claude Code

steps.path: Any session, switched to terminal view
steps.headline: The message box is gone: tap the terminal and your phone's keyboard types straight into Claude Code.
steps.changed: The key row keeps Ctrl, Esc, Tab and Space. Enter and the left/right arrows moved to the D-pad, and Attach (paperclip) and Paste took their places. The message box underneath is hidden in terminal view.
steps.measured: 1 row of 6 keys instead of 7 keys plus the message box; the terminal gains about 64 px of height
steps.notice: Tapping the terminal opens the keyboard; swiping still scrolls. Tapping a key doesn't close the keyboard. When the keyboard opens, Claude Code's window slides up with it. Paste puts your copied text into the terminal; Attach puts the picked file's location in, which Claude Code reads as that file.
steps.risk: Terminal view loses the message box's Stop button (Esc stops Claude instead), voice typing and the model switcher; chat view keeps all three. Android may show a small 'YouCoded pasted from your clipboard' notice when you tap Paste. Typing and the keyboard slide can only be judged on the phone, not in these pictures. A phone browser connected to your computer is unchanged.

steps.path: Any session, terminal view, floating style
steps.headline: The up/down arrows became a D-pad: Send in the middle, left and right on its sides.
steps.changed: Where the up/down pair floated, there is now a plus-shaped pad: Up, Down, Left, Right, and the Send button (your theme's accent colour) in the centre. Send is Enter: it sends what you typed and confirms a menu choice.
steps.measured: 4 arrow keys and Send, 40 px each; the pad covers a 128 px square in the bottom-right corner
steps.notice: One thumb reaches every menu control. The key row is shorter because Enter and the arrows live on the pad now.
steps.risk: The pad covers more of the terminal's bottom-right corner than the old pair, so the end of a long line can sit behind it. Send's arrow looks like the Right arrow beside it; only its colour tells them apart.

steps.path: Any session, terminal view, float style
steps.headline: The same layout in the float style.
steps.changed: The same key row and D-pad as the other two styles.
steps.notice: Nothing specific to this style changes.
